items.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
items.summary: In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magn
items.text:
In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.
Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.
And when you’ve conceded more goals in all competitions this season than anybody else in Europe’s top five leagues, and when you’ve let in more in the league than anybody other than Crystal Palace, it’s pretty obvious that the defence is a major problem. There are serious reasons for concern; a switch of manager alone will not magically save United.
Perhaps Yoro was unfortunate to be sent off. Senne Lammens may have got to the ball ahead of Alexander Isak. But the opposite is also true. Had Yoro not been sent off, it would only have been because Isak’s first touch was heavy. By far the bigger issue as Pochettino prepares for Wednesday’s Champions League game at Sporting and Saturday’s Premier League match at home to Brentford is how easily United were undone by a simple ball over the top. First Matthijs de Ligt, who was much deeper than the rest of the defensive line, inexcusably left it, and then Yoro, in scrambling back, made an appallingly clumsy foul.
De Ligt, who has only been back in training for six weeks as he recovers from a back injury, had not started a league game since November last year. He looked way off the pace, as he had in the defeat to Como, and his selection, in retrospect, was an error by Pochettino. Yoro, who had looked one of United’s better recent signings in his first year after signing from Lille, had become a case study in the damage being part of a dysfunctional team can do to a player: his confidence is shot and he now lurches around like a sad horse, a player who seems always to be at the centre of unfortunate events – such as that header against his own bar against Aston Villa.
There are manifold problems at United, from the leadership to the recruitment to the stadium, but if there is to be an improvement in form, the first thing Pochettino needs to do is to change the mood. This is nothing like a great squad. It is a mess of ideas and strategies, put together over six different managers with no consistent goal in sight. But it is not a squad made up of terrible players. It is a squad made up of players who have lost their way, who had been dragged down into the morass. It’s obvious that United should be better than this, but even this United should be better than this.
United have won only one of 11 games in the league this season, and that was against newly-promoted Ipswich in August. To put that in context, Burnley are the only other side of all 92 in the league not to have won at least twice; when United were relegated in 1973-74, they won three of their first 11 games. Bruno Fernades has now played in four defeats to Liverpool by four goals or more, a record.
It remains, still, almost inconceivable that United will be relegated, or even that they will find themselves in a proper battle. It’s almost a category error; this cannot happen. But there are no terrible sides in the Premier League this season. Perhaps Manchester City’s appeal will fail and their punishment means they will obligingly occupy one of the relegation slots. But the three promoted sides are all showing signs of fight. Crystal Palace will probably improve under Thomas Frank, Sunderland have started keeping clean sheets and are a very different side if Brian Brobbey is fit, Nottingham Forest are far better than their league positions suggests and Fulham are five league games unbeaten.
A bounce will, surely, come at some point under Pochettino but, this season, nothing can be taken for granted at the bottom.

items.text:
Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
November 23, 2026
When India's world chess champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, faced reporters at the pre-tournament press conference in Geneva on Sunday, there was no sign of the youthful, carefree energy one might expect from a 20-year-old.
"I don't think I'm here to defend anything—I'm here to win it all over again," he said.
Starting November 24, Gukesh will be facing challenger Jakhovir Sindarov of Uzbekistan for a purse of $2.5 million (€2.3m) in the World Chess Championship.
Gukesh captured the title in 2024, making him the youngest-ever world champion at just 18. Since then, however, things have not as gone well for the player known for his exceptional calculation skills and a penchant for risky moves. He currently languishes in 26th place in the FIDE world rankings.
The challenger as the favorite
Sindarov, who has climbed to number four in the world, told reporters that he only began training "seriously" last year and has learned a lot from observing the reigning world champion.
"He has a very good strength in typical positions, his calculation is very good, and Gukesh can fight until the end," Sindarov said.
Former world champion Viswanathan Anand, who was also one of the world's best players as a teenager, is not completely surprised by Gukesh's lack of form over the past two years.
"He became the world champion (very young). So suddenly the responsibility is shifted onto you and even expectations," Anand told DW.
"Clearly he has deficiencies in his chess as is normal for someone who's 20, he's not had time to experience a lot."
By the time he became India's first world champion, Anand was 37 – ancient by the age-standards of today's top players.
The computer generation
"With powerful chess software and global connectivity, it is easier for young players today to reach the top level," Jan Gustafsson, coach of Germany's national chess team, told DW.
"Online chess provides many more learning opportunities for talented players," added Gustafsson, who sees the recent movement at the top of the rankings as a "generational shift."
While Norway's Magnus Carlsen, long considered the greatest player of all time, remains number one in the world rankings, he rarely plays classical chess anymore and gave up his world championship title after declining to defend it in 2023.
Now, young players—particularly from Asia—are pushing to the forefront. Alongside Gukesh and Sindarov, players such as Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa from India and Nodirbek Abdusattorov of Uzbekistan—an emerging chess powerhouse—are considered contenders to win a world championship in the not-too-distant future.
"Broad social acceptance and state support ensure that children can focus on chess at a very early stage," Gustafsson said.
Another contender is Germany's Vincent Keymer, who at 22 is number nine in the world and well established among the world's elite. Most recently, Keymer and his teammates won a bronze medal at the World Team Championship, often referred to as the "Chess Olympiad."
Additional reporting by: Thomas Lemmer

items.text:
Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury 'not serious'
- Published
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya's shoulder injury "doesn't look too serious", but he will miss Tuesday's Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta.
Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.
He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula.
"We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging," said Gunners boss Arteta.
"He is not fit [to face Dortmund] but it doesn't look too serious."
Arteta said that while the incident looked pretty innocuous the pain his keeper was in made him fear it was a serious injury.
"With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected," said Arteta.
"When you look at the action it doesn't seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.
"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment.
"The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let's see."
- Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him? 
  - Published1 day ago
Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in their next tranche of matches.
And Raya is huge part of the way that Arsenal play because of his ability with the ball at his feet.
When asked if losing Raya for a long period of time would be the biggest blow to his team, Arteta said: "We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa [Arrizabalaga] and Illan [Meslier].
"Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan."

Raya was forced off in the second half of Saturday’s 2-2 draw with a suspected dislocated shoulder, rais
items.text:
Mikel Arteta is hopeful the shoulder injury David Raya sustained at Newcastle is not too serious but confirmed the goalkeeper would miss Tuesday’s Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund.
Raya was forced off in the second half of Saturday’s 2-2 draw with a suspected dislocated shoulder, raising fears he could be sidelined for an extended period. He had an MRI scan on Arsenal’s return to London and was absent from training on Monday.
Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise at home to Dortmund but Arteta said Raya did not require surgery and could be in contention to face Manchester City on Sunday.
“He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious,” the manager said. “We need some more tests tomorrow, but he’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected. There’s no need of surgery, which was the main fear, especially because I was worried about it for months.”
Asked whether Raya could play at home to City, Arteta said: “Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well. That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and [third-choice] Illan [Meslier]. Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.”
Dortmund are a point behind Arsenal in the Champions League after three wins from their first four matches and Niko Kovac’s side lead Bayern Munich by two points at the top of the Bundesliga. Arteta said a youthful side expected to feature Jobe Bellingham – who was called up by England for the first time last week alongside his brother, Jude – would provide a real test before Real Madrid visit in a fortnight.
“I think you have to congratulate mum and dad for what they’ve done because it’s incredible,” Arteta said of facing the Bellingham brothers in successive Champions League matches. “When you look at the two of them and you put a different shirt on, it’s incredible. But two amazing footballers, what they’re doing is remarkable. So let’s give credit as well to the parents.”

UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa confirms

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.

The four
items.text:
UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa confirms
- Published
England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.
It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.
The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.
The tournament will consist of 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.
The 'All Together' bid included a proposal to use 19 venues, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.
Monday's special meeting of Fifa's Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.
The news comes on the same day the UK government announced a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or be in leadership roles in sport by the time the tournament takes place.
- Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir 
  - Published1 hour ago
Where will matches be held in 2035?
England failed to win the right to host the men's World Cups in 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for the 2030 tournament was abandoned.
But England and Scotland hosted matches at the men's Euros in 2021, and England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.
England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028.
Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.
"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."
The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.
If Manchester United's proposed new Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it would still be considered in its current form.
Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland.
Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.
A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.
Fifa is yet to decide whether all four co-hosts will qualify automatically.
Shaping the future of the game
The participation of women and girls in football has risen by 2.3m since the Women's European Championship was held in England in 2022.
However, women remain significantly underrepresented in leadership positions.
Only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports are held by women and only 12% of sports federations are led by a female.
Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "This is a proud day for Welsh football.
"We've put forward Wrexham and Cardiff as host cities, and it's exciting to think what a World Cup could bring to both cities and the communities around them.
"In Llunio Cymru - our 10-year strategy - we've set ourselves the ambition of reaching the knockout stages in 2035. Some of the players who could take us there are learning the game at clubs across Wales today. Our job is to make sure that wherever a girl grows up in Wales, she can find a team close to home, have a coach who helps her develop and see a route to the Cymru shirt."
Irish Football Association chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country".
"Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that," he added.
Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".
He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."
Fifa's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five. Its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".
That is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.
The bid evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.
"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.
"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."

items.title: ‘Celebrate, inspire, unite’: UK confirmed as host of 2035 Women’s World Cup
items.summary:
The UK is to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup, Fifa has confirmed. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the first World Cup hosted in the country since the 1966 men’s tournament in England.
The UK bid was the only one under consideration for 2035. The 2031 tournament has been awar
items.text:
The UK is to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup, Fifa has confirmed. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the first World Cup hosted in the country since the 1966 men’s tournament in England.
The UK bid was the only one under consideration for 2035. The 2031 tournament has been awarded, also uncontested, to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. The decisions were formalised at a virtual meeting of Fifa’s national associations on Monday.
Debbie Hewitt, the Football Association chair, said of the 2035 World Cup: “Together we will celebrate the power of women’s football, inspire the next generation and unite fans from every corner of the world.”
The UK bid lists 22 stadiums as potential venues. Sixteen are in England, three in Wales, two in Scotland and one is in Northern Ireland. Fifteen host cities are in the running (the bid officially lists 16, counting Trafford as distinct from Manchester).
Andy Burnham said the tournament would bring “visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country”. The prime minister also pointed to the sporting impact, saying it would “bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle”.
Wembley has been proposed for the final, having hosted it at the 2022 Women’s European Championship. Fifa has evaluated 19 stadiums, assessing them as being of “high quality”. All were awarded an score of at least four out of five, except for Elland Road in Leeds (3.9), Easter Road in Edinburgh, Windsor Park in Belfast and Nottingham’s City Ground (all 3.6). Old Trafford has been assessed by Fifa but the proposed new Manchester United stadium could play a significant role instead if built in time.
The three listed stadiums not assessed by Fifa are Birmingham City’s proposed 62,000-seat Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s stadium – which is due two stages of redevelopment – and Chelsea’s stadium because only a redeveloped Stamford Bridge or a new club stadium would come into the picture.
The 22 stadiums will be whittled down to between 14 and 16. The tournament is scheduled to involve 104 matches played by 48 teams over 39 days. The dates are yet to be confirmed but indicative dates of 21 June to 29 July have been informally used as a template during the bidding process.
The tournament is due to be the second Women’s World Cup to include 48 teams, after 2031’s event, mirroring this year’s men’s tournament and making it the largest single-sport event staged in the UK. There are to be 12 groups of four teams followed by knockouts starting with a last 32.
As revealed by the Guardian last week, Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four football associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the tournament.
England, Scotland and Wales are also due to co-host – along with the Republic of Ireland – the men’s European Championship in 2028.

It will take place across 19 stadiums across 15 cities, with one additional host city and three additional stadiums for future consideration.
Presenting the bid at the FIFA meeting, Sky Sports News presenter - and non-executive FA director - Jess Creighton said: "Welcome to your Women's World Cup 2035. A tournament where we want every team, every fan and every nation to feel at home.
"Across the UK, football has always been about bringing people together - and that's why, in 2035, we'll welcome it the way football always has: by helping everyone feel at home.
"Our ambition is to deliver the most-watched FIFA Women's World Cup ever.
"We're predicting in 2035, there will be more than 3.5bn viewers, and over 4.5m tickets sold."
English Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the Congress after the bid's success had been confirmed.
"Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035," Hewitt said.
"We're deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women's football on behalf of the global football family.
"As we said throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women's World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.
"Together, we will celebrate the power of women's football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women's World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women's sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.
"Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle."

items.title: Trump endorses Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, says US has no evidence of wrongdoing
items.summary: On Monday, President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Securit
items.text:
On Monday, President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”
The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk.
In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the Attorney General typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case.
There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.”
Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions.
Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”
Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below.
The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

items.text:
Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard is 'toughest player to play against' right now with Jannik Sinner out of the equation, says Tim Henman
Carlos Alcaraz will head into the 2027 season as the player to beat with Italian Jannik Sinner currently missing from the ATP Tour due to a knee injury; You can watch the Next Gen ATP Finals from 9-13 December in Reggio Calabria, Italy live on Sky Sports Tennis
Monday 23 November 2026 15:20, UK
Carlos Alcaraz is the "toughest player to play against" right now with Jannik Sinner out of the equation, says Tim Henman.
Alcaraz began the year facing questions over his split with long-time coach Juan Carlos Ferrero, but the Spaniard has answered them emphatically by completing the career Grand Slam and adding the elusive ATP Finals title to his collection.
Since returning at the US Open in late August, the 23-year-old has made up for lost time in a superb late-season charge that culminated in Sunday's triumph in Turin, where he beat top-ranked Alexander Zverev in the final.
- Keep track of the full tennis schedule live on Sky Sports
- Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱
By winning the ATP Tour's season-ender, Alcaraz joined Andre Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic as the only men to secure the career Grand Slam and ATP Finals title.
With former world No 1 Jannik Sinner set to undergo surgery on a persistent knee injury in Finland this week, casting doubt over his participation in the Australian Open, Alcaraz looks set to dominate tennis in 2027.
Speaking at the ATP Finals in Turin, former British No 1 Henman told Sky Sports Tennis: "We can obviously have a deep dive into the five matches here, but I think in the context of being out of the game for four and a half months, that is not easy then to come back into a Grand Slam.
"He played well in New York, getting through to the quarter-finals, but then we just have to look at this last third of the season.
"For him to not lose a match, play a couple of matches at Laver Cup, and then he's gone on this tear where every aspect of his game has been so impressive. The physical side of things, the wrist has obviously been perfect.
"Yes, he had a challenge with the hamstring, but mentally and technically his game has been so good. In Paris, he didn't have it all his own way, and I think that was such a good sign that he can play and win with this sort of B or C game.
"He's now come into the Tour-ending championships, the best against the best, an event that he's never won, and he's taken the title."
Henman: A completely different level
Four of the Spaniard's six titles this year have come since he returned from injury, with triumphs in Tokyo and Vienna followed by victories at the Paris Masters and the ATP Finals - all under the guidance of head coach Samuel Lopez and brother Alvaro.
"He started the year off with a bang down in Australia, that was the one Grand Slam that he was missing from his CV," Henman said.
"To be able to achieve the career Grand Slam at such a young age was incredible.
"Then obviously on to the clay, getting injured in Barcelona, missing a big chunk, missing two slams at Roland-Garros and Wimbledon, coming back in New York.
"Zverev's got a better serve than Alcaraz, and he hadn't lost his serve. This is the skill set and the challenge of playing Alcaraz, and I think he's in Zverev's head, obviously, because it was just a completely different level.
"Zverev couldn't find the spots, and then his serve has been unbreakable by everyone else in the tournament, and Alcaraz has dismantled him."
Alcaraz is 'the best'
Former doubles No 1 Jamie Murray said: "He [Alcaraz] is amazing. He is the best. He plays in a completely different way to anything that we see these days on the ATP Tour.
"He obviously came back at the US Open, it's not an easy thing to do. I'm sure he was disappointed losing to [Ben] Shelton, the way that he went out there, but it definitely helped him after that for the rest of the year.
"He was up to speed, he had his rhythm. It's not a huge surprise, because he is one of the two best players in the world, and his level is so much better than everybody else when he's in full flow.
"It's an amazing run that he's won these last three tournaments, but it's not out of the realm of possibility for Carlos Alcaraz to do that."

items.title: Emery insists no change of plan for Aston Villa despite fears over Galatasaray surface
items.summary: Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions Leaguegame at Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface t
items.text:
Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions Leaguegame at Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”.
Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work. Galatasaray played Saturday’s victory over Samsunspor at Basaksehir Fatih Terim stadium, a significantly smaller ground named after the former Turkey manager, who played for and managed Galatasaray.
Galatasaray’s manager, Okan Buruk, acknowledged the pitch would pose problems despite round-the-clock efforts to improve the hybrid surface, where sand remains present. “We are not expecting a perfect pitch, but we are at least expecting a pitch that will be playable and will not get any worse or deteriorate during the game,” he said.
Villa instead trained at Bodymoor Heath, their Warwickshire base, on Monday before flying to Istanbul. Villa typically choose to train there before flying to games overseas, though they trained at Fenerbahce on the eve of their Europa League visit in January, and at Besiktas Park 24 hours before their Europa League triumph in Istanbul in May.
“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery said. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”
The Villa manager added: “If the pitch was not available or a risk for the players, for some injuries, we are not playing there. I think it’s going to be [good] enough, well enough to play the match. We are thinking only to face them [Galatasaray] and thinking only to play how we are, not changing our idea or our plan for the pitch.”
Victor Osimhen is sidelined for Galatasaray with a knee injury, but the record 26-time Turkish champions expect to welcome back the former Tottenham defender Davinson Sánchez. The former Arsenal midfielder Lucas Torreira and Yunus Akgun, who spent 2023-24 on loan at Leicester, scored in the 2-1 win over Samsunspor, which maintained their three-point lead in the Super Lig.
Buruk was sent off after full-time, after receiving a second yellow card for failing to shake hands with the referee, Ali Sansalan, but his touchline ban does not apply to the Champions League. Galatasaray have appealed to the Turkish Football Federation against the dismissal.
“You can shake hands if you want, or not,” Buruk said. “As long as you don’t show disrespect or use abusive language, no one can punish anyone. The referee made a mistake. I expect that mistake to be reversed.”

items.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
items.summary: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the co
items.text:
Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.
The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.
Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.
That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.
Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing, and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.
Startups operating in the CX space have seen multi-million-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion. Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.
During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.

items.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
items.summary: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Ch
items.text:
In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.
The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.
Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 am ET.
In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.
Trump also said the U.S. Attorney General confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.
A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.
The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”
Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.
Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.
“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”
In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
This story is developing...

items.title: PSG had the best attack in Europe but Doué and Kvaratskhelia injuries will test Luis Enrique
items.summary: Luis Enrique is in uncharted territory, even if he insists that “it isn’t a first”. Since arriving at Paris Saint-Germain in 2023, only three players have spent more than 100 days on the sideline – Nuno Mendes, Lucas Hernandez and Presnel Kimpembe – and only Mendes is an important first-team player.
items.text:
Luis Enrique is in uncharted territory, even if he insists that “it isn’t a first”. Since arriving at Paris Saint-Germain in 2023, only three players have spent more than 100 days on the sideline – Nuno Mendes, Lucas Hernandez and Presnel Kimpembe – and only Mendes is an important first-team player. But for the remainder of the season, or at least the vast majority of it, Luis Enrique must do without two of his stars: Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.
Doué arrived in Nice on Saturday evening already bearing scars. The PSG forward wore a mouth guard after Davide Frattesi had dislodged one of his front teeth with a stray arm during France’s defeat by Italy during the international break.
He showed it off to the crowd when he tapped home an Achraf Hakimi cross to give PSG a 2-1 lead a mere 24 seconds after Senny Mayulu had levelled the score from the spot for PSG. Just six minutes later, without making any contact with the oncoming Sofiane Diop, Doué was left screaming on the floor, clutching his right knee.
The Nice players Alidu Seidu and Youssouf Ndayishimiye, both of whom have sustained ACL injuries in recent times, quickly grasped the severity of the injury, the nature of which was confirmed on Sunday. Tests revealed an ACL tear that will probably rule Doué out until the end of the season; Kvaratskhelia suffered the same fate last month.
“We have other players in our squad. We will overcome it as a team,” said Luis Enrique, who added that they are “open” to dipping into the market. Eli Junior Kroupi is being linked with a move from Bournemouth to the Parc des Princes, but should the two-time European champions opt against recruiting this winter, it will be a test of the club’s continued assertion that “the star is the collective”. That mantra belies a continued level of spending at PSG that far outstrips their domestic competitors and an accumulation of talent that led Nice’s manager, Olivier Pantaloni, to describe them as a “club apart” in Ligue 1.
Pantaloni noted PSG’s capacity to turn on “at the press of a button”, which left him in no doubt that PSG would “steamroll” the domestic competition once again this year. His side’s 3-2 defeat at their hands, although valiant, reasserts a hierarchy that no one questions, injuries or no injuries.
Ligue 1 may not challenge PSG but, shorn of two of their most technically gifted players, top European sides will. Even in domestic games, wins have oftentimes relied on call-in-the-cavalry hour, with Ousmane Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia, Vitinha and the like unleashed against already exhausted defences to seal the win. Their victories over Le Mans and Strasbourg, notably, were obtained in this manner.
The serious injuries sustained by Doué and Kvaratskhelia mean there is no longer a cavalry to call upon. PSG will also have to change their contentious policy of resting key players in domestic competition. Will Dembélé have to play more, and can his body sustain it? That is one question among many.
Mika Godts has said he has time on his side to establish himself at PSG. Not any more. Will he step up? Will Ferran Torres, who scored PSG’s third in their 3-2 win against Nice, rediscover his early-season form? Is Mayulu, fresh from making his France debut, ready? Is Nuno Mendes a viable option on the left wing? And can Maghnes Akliouche, who has so quickly curried favour with Luis Enrique, add goals and assists to his impressive performances?
The answers to these questions will determine PSG’s ability to challenge for a third consecutive Champions League title. Diminished in quantity and quality, PSG’s forward line no longer looks the best in Europe.
It was the abject failure of the Neymar-Kylian Mbappé-Lionel Messi frontline that forged the concept of the modern-day PSG. Star quality was not a guarantor of success; the system, it was decided, would be king. In the absence of Doué and Kvaratskhelia, the limits of this accepted truth will be tested this season.
 
Talking points
Several French clubs used the international break to correct their course. Lens called time on the failed Yannick Cahuzac experiment and brought in Didier Digard, fresh from his sacking at bottom side Le Havre. Strasbourg pulled the plug on Hugo Oliveira after 10 games and hired Vítor Matos from Swansea City to become their fourth manager of 2026. Valérien Ismaël has replaced Digard at Le Havre. And Lyon, whose hand was forced by Paulo Fonseca’s wish to manage boyhood club Sporting, welcomed Carlos Vicens, formerly part of Pep Guardiola’s backroom staff.
Vicens was the only manager to secure all three points on his debut, winning 1-0 at Davide Ancelotti’s Lille. In doing so, the Spaniard became the first manager in Lyon’s history to arrive mid-season and beat a top-flight side in his first away match. Lens showed promise in their 1-1 draw against Toulouse but were denied three points by an inspired performance from goalkeeper Guillaume Restes. There are no signs of revival at Le Havre, who lost 3-1 to promoted side Troyes – or at Strasbourg, who were beaten 1-0 by Brest at the Meinau. Chelsea’s partner club currently occupy the relegation playoff spot.
Five consecutive wins in Ligue 1 had lifted spirits in Marseille, but Bruno Génésio had warned that the revival teetered on a “knife’s edge”. An excellent Le Mans exposed their fragility. Goals from Amine Gouiri and Igor Paixão gave Marseille a 2-0 lead only for Le Mans to run riot in the final quarter of the game and win 3-2.
Patrick Videira’s side secured all three points thanks to Jean Vercruysse’s dramatic 95th-minute winner. “There is a global phenomenon of fragility as soon as we concede a goal,” was Génésio’s explanation for Marseille’s collapse. For Videira, Marseille represent the biggest scalp of his managerial career, although draws against Nice, Lens, and Monaco had already shown the club’s ability to compete at this level.
This is an article by Get French Football News

items.text:
Fury vs Joshua undercard: Martin Bakole steps in for Jai Opetaia to fight former heavyweight world champion Deontay Wilder
Martin Bakole will replace Jai Opetaia and fight Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11; Bakole lost to Joseph Parker at short notice and has scored outstanding wins over Tony Yoka, Carlos Takam and Jared Anderson
Monday 23 November 2026 14:30, UK
Martin Bakole will fight Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua on December 11.
Fury and Joshua finally meet after a long-running rivalry in the main event at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.
Wilder is a former WBC heavyweight world champion renowned as one of the hardest punchers in the sport.
He was due to box Australian cruiserweight star Jai Opetaia, who withdrew injured and will now remain in the 200lb division.
Bakole was already scheduled to box on the card and is no stranger to taking a big fight on short notice. He travelled at just three days' notice to step in for Daniel Dubois and box Joseph Parker.
Prior to that Bakole scored outstanding wins over Tony Yoka, Carlos Takam and elite American hope Jared Anderson.
Opetaia's promoter Dana White said: "Jai Opetaia had to withdraw from his fight against Deontay Wilder next month. Stepping in is Martin Bakole, a six-foot-six, 300lb knockout artist who's ready to take on one of the hardest-hitting heavyweights in boxing.
"Wilder and Bakole have 66 wins and 59 knockouts, so you don't want to miss this fight."
Welsh heavyweight Moses Jolly also joins the card in a bout against Igor Adiel Macedo with more bouts still to be announced.

items.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
items.summary: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NV
items.text:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.”
Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director.
In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social, saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair.
“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO.
Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement.
Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence, while industry analysts raised concerns about an outsider replacing him at a time when Nvidia is so critical to the AI boom. Nonetheless, the board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back.

items.title: Raya injury 'not too serious' says relieved Arteta
items.summary:
David Raya injury: Arsenal goalkeeper avoids surgery and blow is not as bad as first feared, says Mikel Arteta
David Raya came off injured during Arsenal's Premier League draw with Newcastle; the Spaniard is the Gunners' undisputed No 1 goalkeeper with Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier as back-up
items.text:
David Raya injury: Arsenal goalkeeper avoids surgery and blow is not as bad as first feared, says Mikel Arteta
David Raya came off injured during Arsenal's Premier League draw with Newcastle; the Spaniard is the Gunners' undisputed No 1 goalkeeper with Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier as back-up options; the 31-year-old got injured at a time where Arsenal have some big games coming up
Monday 23 November 2026 14:42, UK
Mikel Arteta has revealed that David Raya's shoulder injury is not as bad as first feared, but is unsure when the Arsenal goalkeeper will return to action.
Raya came off with a shoulder problem in Saturday's 2-2 draw against Newcastle and there were initial fears that the Spaniard could miss several months if he required surgery.
However, an MRI scan over the weekend has revealed that Raya does not require surgery and while he will miss Tuesday's match with Borussia Dortmund, more scans are needed on Tuesday to understand the full extent of the damage.

- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
"He's not fit for [Dortmund] unfortunately, but it doesn't look too serious," said Arteta.
"We need some more tests tomorrow but it's quite encouraging with the pain he was showing. Immediately the action, we were quite worried but it's not as bad as we expected.
"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first tests we have done showed something much more encouraging. [On Tuesday] we need to ratify that to give you more specifics.
"There was no need for surgery. That was the main fear, because that would have ruled him out for months. Let's see."
Asked if he could return for Arsenal's big Premier League home game with Manchester City on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, Arteta replied: "Tomorrow we will have more tests. Then you will know."
So does Kepa or Meslier play against Dortmund?
Raya's injury means Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier will compete for the goalkeeper spot at Arsenal until the Spain international returns from his injury.
Kepa was widely regarded as Arsenal's No 2 goalkeeper and replaced Raya at Newcastle off the bench.
However, Meslier started against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup fourth round defeat - which was the last time Raya was rotated out the Arsenal starting line-up.
"I think it's clear for us who is going to play tomorrow," said Arteta about who starts out of Kepa and Meslier.
When asked why Meslier started against Fleetwood, Arteta replied: "Because I want everybody to be part of it and to feel part of it. You need to play, and Illan has been really good with us.
"We believe that it was the right thing to share those minutes, the competition. To give a player that every single day is so consistent, so reliable, so supportive, with the rest of the boys, to have the feeling that we trust him as well."
Merson on Raya: Arsenal's next five or six games are crucial
Sky Sports' Paul Merson:
"Raya's injury is a leveller for the other teams - not that much of a leveller because Arsenal still have some good players. When Chelsea miss a key player like that, that's it for them. But I don't think that's the case for Arsenal, they've got a very good squad.
"But that goalkeeper saves you points. That will be the problem for Arsenal.
"The next five or six games for Arsenal are decisive for them. If they come out of this run of games and they are five or six points clear of the pack, it's impossible for anybody to catch them. Every one of their next five or six games is a difficult football match.
"For me, Raya will be a miss. You'd be more comfortable going into those games with him in goal.
"He's the best goalkeeper in the world, by far, at making angles. He reads the game by always making the right angles.
"A lot of people don't see it. When the ball goes back to the goalkeeper, he'll always be on the right angle to get the ball - and then will always play it into the right player's foot.
"If Declan Rice comes short, he'll play it onto his right foot so the ball can go smoothly out to the right-back. All these little things help.
"And now it looks like Kepa is going to come in - and he's not played for a long time. And all these things have to work for him. That could be a worry for Arsenal."

items.title: Manchester United to appeal against Leny Yoro red card in defeat by Liverpool
items.summary: Manchester United intend to appeal against the red card Leny Yoro received in the eighth minute of the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. The defender was dismissed after fouling Alexander Isak outside the penalty area but Mauricio Pochettino believes the striker would not have reached the ball to t
items.text:
Manchester United intend to appeal against the red card Leny Yoro received in the eighth minute of the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. The defender was dismissed after fouling Alexander Isak outside the penalty area but Mauricio Pochettino believes the striker would not have reached the ball to take him through on goal against Senne Lammens and therefore it was not worthy of a sending-off.
United’s head coach said: “I don’t agree because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control. Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul.”
Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick to give Liverpool the lead and Florian Wirtz doubled the lead three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz completed the scoring as Pochettino lost his first game in charge of United, leaving them 19th in the Premier League.
“We’re at the lowest we’ve ever been and no one’s coming to save us,” the midfielder Kobbie Mainoo told MUTV. “There’s no helping hands coming so we’ve got to work together and lean on each other and keep working and hopefully it’ll come good.”
Yoro is due to serve a one-match ban at home to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. He is available for United’s Champions League match at Sporting on Wednesday.

items.text:
This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born.
We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France.
He was the nation’s cover star after that win, variously punching the air, roaring or spreading arms open wide across the front pages of Italy’s sports newspapers. His body language on Sunday night was different. By the end of Inter’s 4-4 draw with Atalanta, Esposito carried the haunted look of a Dickensian protagonist who had just been visited by the ghost of Belgium past.
“I’m really struggling to give an explanation right now,” Esposito told the TV cameras when asked how his team had failed to win a game that they led 2-0, 3-1 and finally 4-2 as late as the 76th minute. “It’s a beautiful thing [to score the hat-trick] but I’m having a hard time enjoying it because we threw two points away.”
A sentiment that can only have been heightened by a sense of history repeating. Esposito’s goals against France had put Italy on course for the quarter-finals of the Nations League. All they needed to do was draw their final group game away to Belgium. Esposito struck again to give them an early lead at the King Baudouin Stadium. And then they collapsed to a 4-1 defeat.
These stories share another recurring character: Charles De Ketelaere. He provided the assists on Belgium’s first and third goals, turning that game on its head in the space of 10 minutes. On Sunday, he was at it again, scoring Atalanta’s second and third goals then winning the penalty from which his teammate Franck Kessié finally equalised in second-half stoppage time.
Even by the standards of this barmy Serie A season, on a weekend that gave us two 5-1 scorelines and a 4-0, this was a preposterous game of football. Inter looked completely in control heading into the final 20 minutes, leading 3-1 thanks to Esposito’s hat-trick.
He might have made it to three before half-time if Marco Sportiello had not denied him from point-blank range when the score was still 1-0. Instead, Esposito had to wait until just after the interval to bag his third, running on to a Marcus Thuram through ball and lifting it over the Atalanta keeper.
None of the three goals were spectacular, but together they illustrated what a menace Esposito has become. For the first, he simply held his spot in the middle of the penalty area after an initial cross was half-cleared, punishing Atalanta’s defence for losing its shape on the second ball. His second was a glancing header at a corner.
In moments like this, it is easy to see why people want to make that link to Vieri, another powerful Inter No 9 who could dominate in the air. But, leaving aside the obvious point that we are comparing a 21-year-old with 13 top-flight goals to a player who won both Serie A’s capocannoniere award and the Pichichi trophy for top scorer in La Liga, is that even the most apt former star to draw parallels with?
Vieri has said that anyone who thinks they are similar “doesn’t understand much about football”, noting that Esposito’s 6ft 3in height and broad-shouldered physique remind him more of Luca Toni.
Esposito’s brothers Salvatore and Sebastiano – both also professional footballers – have compared him to another former Inter player, Edin Dzeko, whom he looked up to while working his way through the club’s academy. There are certainly echoes of the Bosnian in the work he does as an attacking pivot, holding off defenders to make space for runners from midfield.
But Esposito will not be a carbon copy of any player who has gone before him. Part of the thrill of seeing him excel for club and country over the last month has been watching him start to define himself as confidence grows. He played 48 times for Inter last season, yet always was the understudy to Thuram and Lautaro Martínez. This campaign already feels different. He is becoming a main character in his own right.
If only his supporting casts could perform to the same level. Eljif Elmas’s first goal back for Atalanta had been fortuitous, the ball coming back to him after a first scuffed shot was blocked by Federico Dimarco. After Esposito’s third goal, there were 20 minutes in which Maurizio Sarri’s team barely fashioned a chance. Inter contrived to give them a way back in.
De Ketelaere’s first goal came out of the blue, a header from a corner. Was Esposito himself at fault for not being closer to the Belgian as he leapt in a failed attempt to intercept the cross? In any case, Inter responded immediately, Petar Sucic scoring from the penalty spot after Davide Zappacosta fell and handled the ball while trying to cut out a cross from Thuram.
That should have been the end of things, but it wasn’t. Atalanta’s English winger Jonathan Rowe was allowed to twinkle-toe along the byline and flick an outside-of-the-boot pass back to an entirely unmarked De Ketelaere, who smashed home from the middle of the box. Then, in the 90th minute, the Belgian headed the ball on to Alessandro Bastoni’s outstretched arm, earning the spot-kick that Kessié converted.
Had De Ketelaere also fouled Bastoni while challenging for the ball? Inter had a stronger claim that Zappacosta ought to have been shown a red card for his handball. It was the Zappacosta’s blocked cross that wound up falling to Rowe before Atalanta’s third goal.
But Inter’s manager, Cristian Chivu, is not one to indulge that sort of self-pity. His focus after the game was all on his own team’s mistakes, noting that none of the goals they conceded had come in transition but always “a dife

items.title: Kibwana: My Mamdani meeting remarks were about Babu, not Sifuna
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – Former Makueni Governor Kivutha Kibwana has clarified his remarks on the proposed meeting between Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, saying his comments were about Embakasi East MP Babu Owino and not a suggestion that Sifuna should meet the A
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – Former Makueni Governor Kivutha Kibwana has clarified his remarks on the proposed meeting between Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, saying his comments were about Embakasi East MP Babu Owino and not a suggestion that Sifuna should meet the American mayor.
In a post on X, Kibwana said his earlier tweet had been misunderstood, insisting that he was referring to the possibility of Babu, a youthful Nairobi political leader, meeting Mamdani, who is of a similar age and serves as New York City mayor.
“My tweet was about Babu Owino, a Nairobi city chief meeting an agemate Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York. It wasn’t a comment about whom you should meet,” Kibwana said.
Mamdani, who won the New York City mayoral election in November 2025, has attracted international attention for his youthful leadership and progressive political agenda.
He directly addressed Sifuna, expressing confidence in his leadership and warning him against allowing disagreements among supporters to distract him from his political objectives.
“Omwami Edwin Sifuna, we have faith in you. Don’t allow some supporters to detract you. We must keep our eyes on the ball,” he added.
The clarification comes amid debate over Sifuna’s ongoing US tour and suggestions that he should have sought an opportunity to meet Mamdani, who recently made history as New York City’s first Muslim and South Asian mayor.
Sifuna has maintained that his American visit is primarily intended to engage Kenyans living in the diaspora rather than pursue meetings with foreign political leaders.
Speaking during an engagement with Kenyans in Pennsylvania, Sifuna said he would meet Mamdani during a future visit to the United States for the United Nations General Assembly when he scales to presidency.
He explained that his immediate priority was connecting with Kenyans abroad, whom he considers an important constituency in the country’s political landscape.
Sifuna is currently undertaking a two-week tour of the United States, which began on November 21 and is expected to end on December 7, with engagements planned across New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Washington DC, Texas, Washington State and California.
The tour features town hall meetings, church services, business forums, fundraising dinners and engagements with Kenyan professionals and community groups living in the US. He is accompanied by Vihiga Senator Godfrey Osotsi and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, among other members of his delegation.
Sifuna began the tour in New Jersey, where he opened the Linda Mwananchi Movement’s office in Hackettstown before proceeding to Pennsylvania for a church service and a town hall meeting with Kenyans in Allentown on November 22. His itinerary subsequently takes him to Maryland and Washington DC for meetings with business leaders, diaspora groups, women and youth organisations.
He is also scheduled to hold engagements in Dallas and Houston, Texas, before travelling to Washington State, where he will attend church services, a gala dinner and town hall meetings. The final leg of the tour will take him to California, with engagements in San Francisco, Oakland and Silicon Valley before the visit concludes on December 7.
The visit is aimed at popularising the Linda Mwananchi Movement, strengthening its diaspora networks and mobilising financial and political support ahead of the 2027 General Election. It also provides Sifuna with an opportunity to engage Kenyans abroad on governance, the economy and the challenges they face while living outside the country.

items.text:
Watford set to appoint former Romania boss Iordanescu
- Published
Watford are set to appoint Edward Iordanescu as their new manager.
BBC Three Counties Radio report the Romanian is due to become the Hornets' sixth manager inside 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United in his 18th game in charge.
The 48-year-old is understood to be arriving in the UK on Tuesday to sign his contract and plans to bring three members of staff with him and hopes to be in the dugout for Wednesday's Championship fixture at home to Blackburn Rovers (19:45 GMT).
Iordanescu guided Romania at Euro 2024 where they topped their group ahead of Belgium with all four sides ending level on four points from three games before a 3-0 defeat against the Netherlands in the Round of 16.
Iordanescu - whose father Anghel had three spells in charge of the Romanian national team, leading them in two World Cups and two European Championships - left his last role at Polish club Legia Warsaw in October 2025.
It was the 48-year-old's ninth club over a 15-year coaching career which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj among others in his homeland.
Dionisi, who departed with the Hornets in 21st, four points above the relegation zone, was only appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.
Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.
The 46-year-old Italian was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.
The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

He said he was shaving last week when the wat
items.text:
Presidential villa suffers water and power cuts, Nigerian leader says
- Published
Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu says the presidential villa suffers from cuts in electricity and water - issues that are all too common for the country's ordinary citizens.
He said he was shaving last week when the water supply cut at the villa, known as Aso Rock, in Abuja.
He is seeking re-election next January and vowed to address these issues.
Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family in Lagos.
He explained: "On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. In the villa, you won't know punishment dey dia too [there’s punishment there too in Nigerian pidgin].
"The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development. We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria,” he said.
Aso Villa serves as both the office and official residence of the Nigerian president. It is situated at the base of Aso Rock in Abuja.
- Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term? 
  - Published12 November
- Search and rescue teams race against time after Nigeria boat tragedy 
  - Published41 minutes ago
Nigeria has long endured electricity shortages, but recent severe disruptions have been caused primarily by insufficient gas supplies and declining hydropower output, rather than the usual nationwide grid collapse.
Persistent blackouts in Lagos, Abuja and elsewhere have forced distribution companies to implement rotating power cuts, severely impacting households and businesses.
The country also suffers from chronic water shortages, the result of a structural crisis rooted in the gap between rapid urban population growth and decaying, inadequate public water infrastructure, leaving millions without reliable supplies, especially in Lagos.
Tinubu made a high-profile electricity promise during the 2023 election campaign, but the exact wording and how binding it is has become a major point of contention ahead of the election on 16 January 2027.
In 2022, months before the last presidential election, Tinubu said: "Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills any more. A promise made will be a promise kept.
"If I don't keep the promise and I come for a second term, don't vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn't deliver,” he said.
Despite the continuing power cuts, some of his supporters point to improved electricity supplies in rural areas as well as a recently approved $2bn (£1.5bn) investment in a new East–West Super Grid, designed to expand electricity transmission capacity and strengthen the national grid, as evidence that he is doing his best to keep to his promise.
Tinubu defeated the country’s former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as well as former Anambra state governor Peter Obi in 2023 and the three are seen as the strongest contenders once again.

items.title: Man Utd to appeal Yoro red card
items.summary:
Manchester United to appeal Leny Yoro's red card as ex-PL referee Dermot Gallagehr casts his verdict
Manchester United lost 4-0 to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, with Leny Yoro sent off inside the first eight minutes for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity; the club have informed the
items.text:
Manchester United to appeal Leny Yoro's red card as ex-PL referee Dermot Gallagehr casts his verdict
Manchester United lost 4-0 to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, with Leny Yoro sent off inside the first eight minutes for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity; the club have informed the FA of their plans to appeal decision; Dermot Gallagher agreed with the onfield decision
Monday 23 November 2026 12:51, UK
Manchester United have notified the FA of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool.
Mauricio Pochettino's side lost 4-0 at Anfield in the Argentine's first game in charge, and his plans went up in smoke as Yoro was dismissed inside the first eight minutes for bundling over Alexander Isak as the striker ran through on goal.
There was some debate as to whether the foul was a clear denial of the goalscoring opportunity, as it was unclear whether Isak was in control of the ball as he made his way towards the penalty area.
Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations regarding a red card for Denying of an Obvious Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGS), is the likelihood of the attacking player "keeping or gaining control of the ball".
United boss Pochettino felt that not only did Isak lose control of the ball with his touch, but also that United should have been given a penalty for Jeremy Jacquet's challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments before.
However, former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher backed the onfield decision in both instances.
